::::: {.blog-docs}

## During the build and in the browser

A build may run R/Python code to compute a figure or derived dataset, or reuse a saved result. After publication, Mermaid diagrams, interactive maps, and Observable JS controls run in the reader's browser.

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-cap: "Computation during publication and interaction during reading are different workloads."
flowchart TD
    subgraph CI["At build time"]
      A["R / Python analysis"] --> B["Quarto HTML + assets"]
    end
    subgraph BROWSER["In the visitor's browser"]
      C["Rendered prose + charts"]
      D["Mermaid diagrams"]
      E["Observable JS controls"]
      F["Interactive maps"]
    end
    B --> C
    B --> D
    B --> E
    B --> F
```

## Components used on this website

:::: {.docs-card-grid}
::: {.docs-card}
### Theme and layout

[Sketchy](https://bootswatch.com/sketchy/) supplies the base theme. `misc/theme-light.scss` and `misc/theme-dark.scss` define the light and dark palettes, including the red navigation bar. `misc/styles.css` uses a system font for reading surfaces while retaining Sketchy's headings and controls.
:::
::: {.docs-card}
### Mermaid

Flowcharts and sequence diagrams are written in Quarto code cells and rendered as SVG diagrams in the browser. Their colors follow the active light or dark theme.
:::
::: {.docs-card}
### Observable JS

Reactive controls can update a table or visualization without rerunning scientific Python/R code on a server. Try the [freeze scenario explorer](freeze.qmd).
:::
::: {.docs-card}
### Spatial interaction

Individual research posts can embed interactive geographic outputs produced by packages such as `tmap` and JavaScript mapping libraries.
:::
::: {.docs-card}
### Comments

[GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/YONGHUNI/blog/discussions) back the Giscus comment UI included through shared Quarto metadata.
:::
::: {.docs-card}
### Publishing metadata

The custom [Lua filter](https://github.com/YONGHUNI/blog/blob/main/misc/quarto-version.lua) supports the Quarto version annotation in the site's footer.
:::
::::

## Quarto components

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Diagram

```text
Quarto's {mermaid} code cells
→ diagram in the published HTML
→ no hand-maintained PNG export
```

The diagrams in these docs use Quarto's native Mermaid integration.

### Tabbed content

```markdown
## Configuration {.panel-tabset}

### Nix
Pinned tools and CLI.

### Pixi
Shared R/Python runtime.
```

Tabs group related examples within a page. The sidebar links to the separate guides.

### Reactive widgets

```text
Observable input changes
→ dependent OJS cells update
→ visitor sees new result
```

This site's [interactive freeze explorer](freeze.qmd) uses built-in Observable Inputs; it does not call a server or access private infrastructure.

:::

## Layout and navigation

These guides share a docked sidebar and an in-page table of contents where screen space allows. The overview cards switch to one column on narrow screens. Top-down flowcharts reduce the need to shrink diagrams to fit the page; longer sequence diagrams still need more horizontal space.

Quarto provides the diagrams, tabs, and Observable JS integration. The documentation does not add a separate site-wide JavaScript framework. The [source repository](https://github.com/YONGHUNI/blog) contains the current settings and styles.
